chapter: Chicago friends: Tesch, Stacy and Wettling
title: Tesch and Bix living for music; Maugham's beachcomber
summary: Freeman says Tesch lived jazz deeply, young players wrongly imitated Bix's life, and compares them to Maugham's beachcomber killed by beauty.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: You wanted to talk about Teschemacher, I can tell you that no one lived jazz music more deeply than Teschemacher. He really loved it and his whole life was music, and I think that he, as I say, had he not been in that accident, I think he died when he was about 28 -- I am not sure of that age, but it seemed to me he was in his late twenties -- he would have gone on to become one of the greats.

Although he had a great regard -- he idolized Benny Goodman, he was not influenced by Benny Goodman. He was influenced, as I said, by Louis, by Bix, by Jimmy Noone, by many of the great black players of that day, by Omer Simeon who was a great clarinet player with --
With Earl, but before that, on the records of Jelly Roll Morton.
Well, it was sad, but Tesh, I think

really in the short time that he lived, lived a beautiful life in that he just lived music and you see, he idolized - as young people, we had a tendency, we were naive and instead of just idolizing the musicality of our idols, we wanted to live like them and I think that was a great mistake, because in following Bix' life, I think that most cornet players, trumpet players were ruined by him because they all became drunkards, you see, Bix -- it wasn't music that made Bix a drunk. Bix was just a dip-somaniac, as I said earlier, because Bix was also a very profound man.

And Bix was an educated man and he had great regard for the theatre, books, for anything artistic. It wasn't just music, but in the short time that Tesh and Bix were to live, they lived full lives, if being dedicated to music can be considered a full life, and I certainly would agree that it can be.

I always think of this analogous thing that Somerset Maugham wrote about a man who lived as a beach-comber on a beautiful island and when someone asked the writer how the man died, or why he died, he said, 'I think it was the beauty of it all that killed him.'
And, you know, there is much to be said for that line because I have seen that happen to people. They just die from living perhaps too beautiful, too dreamlike, too

fantastic a life.
But Then again, that could sound a little naive.
Who knows what prolongs a person's life, who knows what
cuts a life short, excepting that these men burned them-
selves out at an early time, just staying up all night
drinking.
